text:
A: Hi! Hello, can you hear me?
B: Yeah, fine. Gareth.
A: Chiara! Nice to meet you. I have to say, I put on my form that you looked very organised. The files, the map.
B: [laughs] Everyone's been very kind about those files. A graduate labelled them. I just put them on the shelf.
A: Okay, but you chose the graduate, so it still counts, no?
B: I'll take that. Where are you?
A: Fulham. And you're in... Kent?
B: Maidstone, yeah. Civil engineer. Drainage and flood risk.
A: Flood risk! Sorry, so you stop floods?
B: Sort of. I try to stop people building in the wrong places, and when something does flood I go out and work out why. There's a lot of standing in fields.
A: My grandmother's village near Turin flooded, the Po, years ago. She still talks about it. The water came right up to the church steps. Erm, sorry, that's not a question. What I mean is, I think it's an important job.
B: No, that's exactly the sort of thing. People don't think about drainage until it's in their kitchen.
A: Literally. And me, I was in brand partnerships at a luxury label, and now I'm consulting, sort of. Freelance strategy. Between roles. Does that make sense?
B: Yeah. Is it going alright?
A: Erm. Honestly? Up and down. Some days it's lovely, and some days I'm on the sofa refreshing LinkedIn. Sorry, that's very honest.
B: That's fine. I think I'd go a bit mad without work, to be fair. I'd end up fixing the shed full-time.
A: [laughs] Is the shed bad?
B: It's got a tree growing through it.
A: No!
B: Small tree. Sapling.
A: Okay, that's still a tree. Do you travel? Sorry, I always ask everyone this.
B: Bit. Lake District, Cornwall, once the Dordogne. Somewhere warm every couple of years for my lad.
A: I love the Dordogne. But I'm terrible with flying. I get so anxious with the connections, I check the gate every five minutes.
B: I'm the opposite. My partner, Claire, says it's infuriating. The flight's delayed four hours and I'm just sat there with a pint.
A: That's so British. I would be crying at the desk.
B: [laughs] Somebody has to cry at the desk, I suppose.
A: Exactly! And food, do you cook? Sorry, I'm obsessed with food.
B: Weekends, yeah. A roast on Sunday, a big chilli on Saturday. I've got a barbecue I'm a bit too proud of.
A: A man with a barbecue. Okay. I make my nonna's agnolotti every Sunday, all by hand, and my husband, Tom, he works at a City law firm, he just sits and eats. He doesn't help.
B: Sounds about right. That's what I'd do, given the chance.
A: [laughs] You would sit and eat?
B: I'd offer to wash up. Eventually.
A: Eventually! Claire must be very—
